decision: How should the village fund the leaking hall roof?
context: The village hall roof needs 48,000 to repair and leaks into the main room each winter. The parish reserve holds 31,000, a grant of up to 20,000 needs a 12-month application, and a loan costs 5 percent a year. Two weddings and a clinic are booked in the hall over the next 5 months.

options.name: reservepatch
options.text: Spend 31,000 of the reserve on a partial repair of the worst sections

options.name: waitgrant
options.text: Apply for the 20,000 grant and patch temporarily for another year

options.name: takeloan
options.text: Borrow the shortfall and complete the whole repair this spring

options.name: fundraise
options.text: Run a six-month local appeal and repair after the summer bookings

decision: How should the bakery handle a failing starter?
context: A small bakery's main sourdough starter has turned sluggish, and loaves now rise 30 percent less than usual. It supplies 6 cafes on standing weekly orders worth 1,400. A backup starter in the fridge is 9 days old and untested at scale, and a baker friend offers a jar of her own culture.

options.name: revivemain
options.text: Feed the main starter twice daily and sell fewer loaves for a week

options.name: usebackup
options.text: Switch production to the fridge backup and accept some uneven batches

options.name: friendjar
options.text: Take the friend's culture and rebuild the recipe around its timing

options.name: commercial
options.text: Add a pinch of baker's yeast to every loaf until the starter recovers

decision: How should the clinic reduce walk-in overcrowding?
context: A community clinic sees 70 walk-ins on Mondays, with waits up to 3 hours, while Wednesday has only 25. Two of its 5 nurses prefer fixed appointments, and about a third of patients have no phone for booking. Staff time is fixed and no new hires are possible this year.

options.name: bookedslots
options.text: Switch Mondays to booked slots with a small walk-in reserve

options.name: triagenurse
options.text: Place one nurse at the door to triage and redirect low-urgency cases

options.name: shiftdays
options.text: Advertise Wednesday as the preferred walk-in day and add a Monday cap

options.name: textqueue
options.text: Offer a remote queue by text so patients can wait at home

decision: How should the class trip transport be arranged?
context: Year 5 has 54 pupils going to a science museum 90 km away on a fixed date. A chartered coach costs 1,150, two parent-driven minibuses cost 380 in fuel but need 6 extra DBS-cleared adults, and the train costs 840 with one change. The school budget for the trip is 900.

options.name: charter
options.text: Hire the chartered coach and ask families to cover the gap

options.name: minibuses
options.text: Use two minibuses driven by vetted parent volunteers

options.name: traintrip
options.text: Take the train and reduce the group to the museum's 40-pupil cap

options.name: localvisit
options.text: Replace the trip with a visit closer to school at 300 total

decision: What should the team do about a flaky test suite?
context: About 8 percent of CI runs fail on tests that pass when rerun, costing roughly 25 developer-minutes each. The team has 6 developers and a release due in 3 weeks. A full fix of the worst 15 tests is estimated at 6 developer-days.

options.name: quarantine
options.text: Move the flaky tests into a non-blocking quarantine job today

options.name: fixworst
options.text: Spend 6 days fixing the 15 worst tests before the release

options.name: autoretry
options.text: Add automatic reruns of failures and track the retry rate

options.name: rotatingowner
options.text: Assign one developer each week to own test health alongside features

decision: What should the farm do about rising feed prices?
context: A farm with 40 milking goats pays 4,800 a month for feed, up 22 percent this year. Pasture can cover about half the herd's needs from April to October, but yields drop on the hillside plots. Selling 8 goats would cut feed costs by 20 percent, and a neighbour offers hay at a fixed price for 12 months.

options.name: sellgoats
options.text: Sell the 8 lowest-yielding goats to reduce the herd's feed needs

options.name: fixedhay
options.text: Sign the neighbour's 12-month fixed-price hay supply contract now

options.name: morepasture
options.text: Fence and reseed a further 3 hectares of pasture for the herd

options.name: cutration
options.text: Trim the concentrate ration slightly and accept lower milk volume

decision: How should the family cover Saturday sports and music?
context: Two parents have children aged 7 and 10, with football at 9:00 across town and a music lesson at 9:30 near home. One parent works every second Saturday. A neighbour can drive on alternate weeks, and moving the music lesson to Sunday costs an extra 8 per lesson.

options.name: neighbourswap
options.text: Take turns with the neighbour driving and share the cost of fuel

options.name: movesunday
options.text: Move music to Sunday and pay the surcharge for each lesson

options.name: dropfootball
options.text: Pause football for the term and keep the music lesson only

options.name: splitparents
options.text: Plan the parents' rota around the rest days and swap when needed

decision: How should the lab respond to an aging freezer?
context: A minus-80 freezer holding 11 years of samples is 14 years old and has had two temperature alarms this quarter. A replacement costs 9,500 with a 5-week delivery, and the lab has one spare unit that is already 70 percent full. Roughly 15 percent of the samples are irreplaceable.

options.name: buynew
options.text: Order a replacement now and migrate everything on arrival

options.name: splitsamples
options.text: Move the irreplaceable samples into the spare and keep the rest

options.name: serviceold
options.text: Pay for a service visit and monitor the old unit more closely

options.name: offsite
options.text: Rent space at a partner institution's cold store for key samples

decision: How should the youth club set its season fees?
context: A youth football club has 92 players and a 14,000 annual budget, with fees currently 120 per child. Pitch hire rises by 2,100 next season, and 18 families already get a reduced rate. Last time fees rose by 25 percent, 9 players left.

options.name: flatrise
options.text: Raise every fee to 145 and keep the discount scheme unchanged

options.name: tiered
options.text: Introduce income-based tiers, with higher fees for those who can pay

options.name: sponsor
options.text: Keep fees flat and look for a local sponsor to cover the 2,100

options.name: fewerpitch
options.text: Keep fees flat and cut pitch hours by moving training to a school hall

decision: How should the branch library change opening hours?
context: A branch library is open 6 days for 38 hours, with a council cut requiring 6 fewer hours a week. Evenings after 5 pm draw 22 percent of visits, Saturdays 18 percent, and school-day mornings are quietest at 9 percent. Volunteers could run a short Saturday session.

options.name: closemornings
options.text: Close school-day mornings and keep evenings and weekends

options.name: closeday
options.text: Close one full weekday and keep the remaining hours the same

options.name: volunteersat
options.text: Keep Saturday through volunteers and cut staffed hours elsewhere

options.name: shortenall
options.text: Trim an hour from every day so no group loses a full session

decision: Which route should the workshop take for the lathe?
context: A woodworking shop's only lathe broke a bearing and a repair quote is 1,350 with a 3-week wait. A used replacement lathe at 2,200 is available now, and a new one costs 4,900. The lathe accounts for about 30 percent of weekly income of 3,200.

options.name: repair
options.text: Pay for the repair and outsource urgent turning in the meantime

options.name: usedlathe
options.text: Buy the used lathe immediately and keep the old one for parts

options.name: newlathe
options.text: Order the new lathe on finance and accept the delivery delay

options.name: rentlathe
options.text: Rent a lathe from a nearby makerspace for the 3 weeks

decision: What should the council do with a loss-making bus route?
context: A rural bus route carries 140 passengers a week and costs 15,000 a year more than it takes in. 60 percent of riders are over 65, and the nearest alternative is a taxi service costing 12 each way. The council must cut 40,000 across transport this year.

options.name: dropbus
options.text: Withdraw the route and fund subsidised taxi vouchers instead

options.name: cutfrequency
options.text: Halve the frequency and keep the route running on fewer days

options.name: communityvan
options.text: Replace the bus with a volunteer-driven community minibus

options.name: keepbus
options.text: Keep the route and take the savings from other transport lines

decision: How should the team move the old customer database?
context: A 400 GB customer database runs on a server out of vendor support in 4 months. A managed cloud service costs about 900 a month, a new in-house server about 6,000 once, and a vendor-supported upgrade 3,500 a year. The team has two engineers and no dedicated database administrator.

options.name: managed
options.text: Move to the managed cloud service with a one-time migration

options.name: newserver
options.text: Buy a new in-house server and migrate the data themselves

options.name: vendorupgrade
options.text: Pay for the vendor-supported upgrade and stay on the same system

options.name: trimfirst
options.text: Archive old records first and then decide where the smaller set goes

decision: What should the market stall do with surplus tomatoes?
context: A stall has 220 kg of ripe tomatoes that will not last past Friday, and normal weekend sales take about 90 kg. A canning session uses a rented kitchen at 60 an hour and yields 40 jars per hour. A restaurant offers 2 per kg for 60 kg, and a food bank can collect free.

options.name: cannerun
options.text: Rent the kitchen and make sauce jars to sell over autumn

options.name: sellrestaurant
options.text: Sell 60 kg to the restaurant at the discount price offered

options.name: donatefood
options.text: Donate the surplus to the food bank and take the goodwill

options.name: markdown
options.text: Cut the stall price by a third to move more at the weekend

decision: Where should the community choir hold its winter concert?
context: The choir has 45 singers and expects 150 to 250 audience members. The church seats 180 at 150 hire, the school hall seats 260 at 400, and a care-home lounge seats 70 for free but would host two performances. A previous concert in the church raised 900 in donations.

options.name: church
options.text: Book the church and cap the audience at its seating limit

options.name: schoolhall
options.text: Book the school hall to fit the whole expected audience

options.name: carehome
options.text: Perform twice at the care-home lounge for residents and families

options.name: outdoor
options.text: Hold it outdoors in the park and accept the weather risk

decision: Which route should the group take on day three?
context: A group of 8 hikers reaches a junction with 5 hours of daylight left. The ridge route is 14 km with views and exposure to a forecast wind of 50 km/h, the valley route is 17 km and flat but muddy, and a bus down the valley leaves at 3 pm. One member has a sore knee.

options.name: ridge
options.text: Take the ridge route and turn back if the wind increases

options.name: valley
options.text: Take the valley route and accept the mud and extra distance

options.name: latebus
options.text: Catch the 3 pm bus and skip most of the day's walking

options.name: splitgroup
options.text: Split into two groups with a regroup point at the hut

decision: How should the library run its new seed collection?
context: A library received 3,000 donated seed packets and wants to lend them to residents. Staff time for the project is limited to 4 hours a week. Seeds from open-pollinated plants can be saved and returned, while a share of the donated packets are hybrids that will not breed true.

options.name: catalogue
options.text: Catalogue every packet and loan them out like books

options.name: selfservice
options.text: Set up a self-service cabinet and ask users to leave a note

options.name: gardenclub
options.text: Hand the collection over to a local gardening club to manage

options.name: seasonal
options.text: Release seeds in three seasonal batches with planting talks

decision: How should the small office back up its files?
context: A 12-person office holds 2 TB of shared files on one network drive. A cloud backup costs 70 a month, a pair of rotated external disks costs 300 once but needs someone to swap them weekly, and a second office drive costs 600. The last file loss, two years ago, cost about 3 days of work.

options.name: cloud
options.text: Pay for the cloud backup with automatic daily offsite copies

options.name: rotated
options.text: Use two external disks swapped each Friday by a named person

options.name: seconddrive
options.text: Install a second drive that mirrors the first one overnight

options.name: combo
options.text: Use a second drive plus a monthly cloud snapshot of key folders

decision: How should the art teacher use the single studio?
context: A school has one art studio used by 14 classes a week, and the sculpture club wants two afternoon slots. Kiln firings need 8 hours once a week, and pupils from 3 classes complain of crowded sessions. Two spare rooms exist but have no sinks.

options.name: clubslots
options.text: Give the sculpture club two afternoon slots and trim class time slightly

options.name: sparerooms
options.text: Use the spare rooms for dry lessons and keep wet work in the studio

options.name: capclasses
options.text: Cap class sizes at 20 and run extra sessions where possible

options.name: noclub
options.text: Decline the club request and protect the timetabled class time

decision: How should the beekeeper prepare the weak hives?
context: A beekeeper has 12 hives, and 3 are weak, with fewer than 15,000 bees going into winter. Combining the weak hives loses their queens but boosts survival odds, feeding syrup costs about 25 per hive, and leaving them risks losing all three. Honey income from a strong hive is around 180 a year.

options.name: combine
options.text: Combine the three weak hives into the strong ones

options.name: feedsyrup
options.text: Feed the weak hives syrup and insulate them for winter

options.name: leavenat
options.text: Leave them alone and accept whatever survives the winter

options.name: pairup
options.text: Pair the weak hives beside a strong one to share warmth

decision: How many copies should the zine print?
context: A local zine editor has sold out 400 copies of each of the last two issues within 6 weeks. Printing 400 costs 520, 800 costs 760, and a print-on-demand service costs 3.10 a copy with no stock. The editor has 300 in savings and pre-orders so far total 110.

options.name: fourhundred
options.text: Print 400 copies as before and keep the upfront cost down

options.name: eighthundred
options.text: Print 800 copies to get the lower unit cost per copy

options.name: ondemand
options.text: Use print-on-demand and accept a higher price per copy

options.name: preorders
options.text: Open pre-orders for two weeks and print exactly what sells

decision: How should the clinic deliver the seasonal vaccine?
context: A clinic has 600 doses for a catchment of 2,400 people, with a priority group of about 500. Drop-in clinics bring crowds, mailed appointments for the priority group cost 1.20 each, and a mobile team could visit two care homes. Only 55 percent of past invitees attended.

options.name: dropin
options.text: Run drop-in clinic days and give doses in order of arrival

options.name: invitepriority
options.text: Send invitations to the priority group by mail and book slots

options.name: mobileteam
options.text: Send the mobile team to care homes first and then open the clinic

options.name: pharmacies
options.text: Share half the doses with two local pharmacies to widen access

decision: How should the garden centre staff the spring rush?
context: A garden centre does 40 percent of its yearly sales in 8 weeks. Two permanent staff handle normal weeks, and spring needs about 120 extra hours a week. Agency staff cost 17 an hour, trainees for local students 12 an hour but need 2 weeks of training, and longer opening hours cost 600 in utilities.

options.name: agency
options.text: Hire agency staff for the 8 weeks at the higher hourly rate

options.name: students
options.text: Recruit and train local students at the lower hourly rate

options.name: overtime
options.text: Pay the two permanent staff overtime and extend opening hours

options.name: onlineorders
options.text: Move some sales to online pre-orders with a collection window

decision: How should the food pantry spend a 5,000 gift?
context: A food pantry serves 180 households a month and has received an unrestricted 5,000 gift. Its chest freezer is failing, its dry goods run out by the third week of each month, and a van lease expires in 4 months. Fresh produce donations are growing but spoil without cold storage.

options.name: freezer
options.text: Buy a commercial freezer and cooler to store fresh produce

options.name: drygoods
options.text: Spend the gift on dry goods to cover the week-three shortfall

options.name: vandeposit
options.text: Put the gift toward a deposit on a new delivery van lease

options.name: splitgift
options.text: Divide the gift across the freezer, dry goods and van fund

decision: How should the lab share its survey data?
context: A research group holds survey data from 1,200 respondents who consented to academic use only, with some free-text answers that could identify them. A funder asks for open access within 12 months. Cleaning the free text would take about 3 weeks of a postdoc's time.

options.name: openclean
options.text: Clean the free text and publish the data openly online

options.name: controlled
options.text: Deposit it in a repository with controlled access on request

options.name: summaryonly
options.text: Publish only aggregate tables and the analysis code itself

options.name: askfunder
options.text: Ask the funder for an exemption and keep the data internal

decision: How should the tool library handle damaged tools?
context: A tool library has 320 items and about 40 returned damaged each year, mostly by new members. Repairs cost an average of 18 each, a deposit scheme would add friction, and the library has 6 regular volunteers. Membership is 210 and growing by 5 a month.

options.name: deposit
options.text: Take a refundable deposit on higher-value tools only

options.name: repaircafe
options.text: Hold a monthly repair session for the volunteers and members

options.name: trainfirst
options.text: Require a short induction before borrowing any power tools

options.name: feeincrease
options.text: Raise the annual membership fee to cover the repair costs

decision: How should the on-call team fix noisy alerts?
context: An on-call team of 7 receives about 60 alerts a week, and 70 percent need no action. Two real outages in the past year were buried among the noise. Reworking the rules would take about 10 engineer-days, and a vendor tool that groups alerts costs 400 a month.

options.name: rewrite
options.text: Spend the 10 days rewriting and deleting the alert rules

options.name: vendortool
options.text: Buy the grouping tool and leave the existing rules alone

options.name: pagetiers
options.text: Page only for top-tier alerts and send the rest to email

options.name: rotate
options.text: Rotate a single weekly triage owner to clean up as they go

decision: What should the cheesemaker do with the new batch?
context: A cheesemaker has 120 wheels that are 5 months old and could age to 12 months. Sold now they bring 9 each from a wholesaler, and aged they bring 15 each but tie up the cave space for 7 months and risk 10 percent loss. A bank loan payment of 2,800 is due in 6 weeks.

options.name: sellnow
options.text: Sell all the wheels now to cover the loan payment

options.name: ageall
options.text: Age all the wheels and borrow against them for the payment

options.name: halfhalf
options.text: Sell half now and age the other half to full maturity

options.name: directsale
options.text: Sell at the weekend market at 12 each as a medium-aged cheese

decision: What should the traveller do after a missed connection?
context: A traveller misses the last connection to a city 400 km away, arriving at 11 pm. The airline offers a hotel and a flight tomorrow at 10 am, a night coach leaves at 1 am for 38, and a rental car costs 120 plus fuel. An interview starts at 9:30 tomorrow morning.

options.name: airlineflight
options.text: Accept the hotel and the 10 am flight and email the interviewers

options.name: nightcoach
options.text: Take the 1 am coach and arrive with some sleep before the interview

options.name: rentalcar
options.text: Rent a car and drive through the night to arrive on time

options.name: reschedule
options.text: Ask to reschedule the interview and take the airline's offer

decision: How should the town schedule its summer festival?
context: A town festival draws about 6,000 visitors across 2 days and costs 24,000. Hotels are fully booked on the traditional weekend, which is also the week of local exams. Moving it a month earlier risks cooler weather, and a two-weekend format would double costs for stalls.

options.name: sameweekend
options.text: Keep the traditional weekend and ask schools to adjust the exams

options.name: earliermonth
options.text: Move it a month earlier and add a covered tent for cover

options.name: twoweekends
options.text: Split it across two weekends with a smaller programme each

options.name: latersummer
options.text: Move it to late summer when the hotels have spare rooms

decision: How should the council shorten the allotment waiting list?
context: A town has 140 allotment plots and a waiting list of 260 people, with an average wait of 6 years. A third of plots are held by tenants who visit rarely, and splitting plots in half would cost 40 each in fencing. A disused field of 1.5 hectares could host 60 new plots but needs drainage costing 22,000.

options.name: splitplots
options.text: Halve the largest plots and offer the halves to those waiting

options.name: reclaimidle
options.text: Reclaim plots from inactive tenants after a warning period

options.name: drainfield
options.text: Drain the disused field and open it up as 60 new plots

options.name: sharescheme
options.text: Pair people on the list with tenants who need help on plots

options.name: capterms
options.text: Introduce 5-year terms with renewal on proof of regular use

decision: What should the bakery do about its failing deck oven?
context: A bakery's deck oven fails to hold temperature about twice a month, ruining roughly 60 loaves each time. A technician quotes 2,100 for a repair expected to last 2 years, a new oven costs 14,500, and a used oven at 6,000 is 8 years old. Monthly profit averages 3,300.

options.name: repairoven
options.text: Pay the 2,100 repair and keep monitoring the oven closely

options.name: newoven
options.text: Buy the new oven on a 3-year payment plan from the supplier

options.name: usedoven
options.text: Buy the used oven and keep the old oven on hand as a spare

options.name: rentbake
options.text: Rent oven time at a neighbouring bakery for the busiest days

options.name: smallerrange
options.text: Narrow the range to the products that bake reliably in it

decision: How should the school launch its mentoring scheme?
context: A secondary school wants to pair 60 struggling Year 9 pupils with mentors. It has 12 sixth-form volunteers, 8 teachers offering one lunchtime a week, and a local firm offering 15 staff for an hour a fortnight. Past peer schemes lost half their pairs within a term.

options.name: sixthform
options.text: Use the sixth-form volunteers in small groups of five pupils

options.name: teachers
options.text: Use the teachers one-to-one and limit the scheme to 8 pupils

options.name: firmstaff
options.text: Use the firm's staff for the pupils with the highest need

options.name: mixedmodel
options.text: Combine all three groups with a coordinator and weekly checks

options.name: pilotclass
options.text: Pilot with one class of 28 pupils and expand it next term

decision: How should the team change a widely used API?
context: A public API has about 300 integrations, and a field's meaning must change because of a data model fix. A new version number costs two years of parallel support, a breaking change in place affects an estimated 40 clients, and an additive field avoids the break but leaves confusing docs.

options.name: newversion
options.text: Release a new API version and support both for two years

options.name: breakinplace
options.text: Make the change in place with 90 days' notice to clients

options.name: addfield
options.text: Add a new, correctly named field and deprecate the old one

options.name: flagparam
options.text: Add an opt-in request flag that switches to the new meaning

options.name: migrateclients
options.text: Contact the 40 affected clients and migrate them one by one

decision: How should the orchard respond to a late frost forecast?
context: An orchard has 1,200 trees in full blossom and a forecast of minus 2 degrees for two nights. Frost fans cost about 800 to rent per night, smudge pots 350 per night for the most exposed block, and spray-on frost protection 500 for the whole orchard but has mixed reliability. Expected fruit income is 38,000.

options.name: rentfans
options.text: Rent frost fans for both nights across the whole orchard

options.name: smudgepots
options.text: Burn smudge pots in the most exposed block of trees only

options.name: sprayprotect
options.text: Apply the spray-on frost protection on all trees tonight

options.name: insureonly
options.text: Do nothing and claim on the crop insurance if it is damaged

options.name: sprinklers
options.text: Run the overhead sprinklers through the night on every block

decision: How should the small museum change its entry pricing?
context: A museum with 28,000 yearly visitors charges 8 a ticket and has a deficit of 30,000. A free-entry weekend could raise footfall by 40 percent but cut ticket income, a 3 increase risks losing school groups, and a membership scheme at 35 needs marketing effort.

options.name: raise3
options.text: Raise the ticket price by 3 and keep school rates

options.name: freeweekend
options.text: Offer free entry on weekends and ask for donations

options.name: membership
options.text: Launch a 35 yearly membership with unlimited visits

options.name: timedslots
options.text: Introduce timed slots with higher prices at peak hours

options.name: grantroute
options.text: Keep prices and apply for a cultural operating grant

decision: How should the club fix its cold meeting room?
context: A hobby club of 30 members meets in a rented room that stays at 11 degrees in winter, and 5 older members have stopped attending. The landlord allows a portable heater with an electrical check at 90. Moving to a heated room across town costs 15 more per session and cuts the time slot by 30 minutes.

options.name: heaters
options.text: Buy two portable heaters and pay for the electrical check

options.name: moveroom
options.text: Move to the heated room and absorb the added session cost

options.name: blankets
options.text: Provide blankets and hot drinks and change nothing else

options.name: daytime
options.text: Shift the meetings to afternoons when the room is warmer

options.name: negotiate
options.text: Ask the landlord to heat the room in exchange for higher rent

decision: What should the pottery do about a bad glaze batch?
context: A pottery found that a new glaze, used on 140 mugs, crazes after a few washes. Refiring costs about 2 per piece and may not work, reselling as seconds earns 40 percent of the normal 14 price, and recalling sold units would cost about 600. Half the mugs are already in 5 shops.

options.name: refire
options.text: Refire the mugs after applying a corrected glaze coating

options.name: sellseconds
options.text: Sell the affected mugs as discounted seconds at a lower price

options.name: recall
options.text: Recall the mugs already sold and refund the five shops

options.name: scrapall
options.text: Destroy the whole batch and re-make the order from scratch

options.name: warnshops
options.text: Inform the shops and let them decide on their remaining stock

decision: How should the clinic handle missed appointments?
context: A clinic has a 17 percent no-show rate across 120 weekly slots, with the highest rates among patients under 30. Reminder texts cost 0.05 each and reduce misses by about a quarter, double booking raises waits on busy days, and a cancellation fee would deter some vulnerable patients.

options.name: textreminders
options.text: Send reminder texts two days and two hours before each slot

options.name: overbook
options.text: Overbook slots by 10 percent in the highest-risk sessions

options.name: noshowfee
options.text: Charge a small fee to patients who miss an appointment

options.name: waitinglist
options.text: Keep a same-day waiting list to fill any cancelled slots

options.name: openaccess
options.text: Move younger patients to open sessions that need no booking

decision: What should the shop owner do about the lease renewal?
context: A bookshop has a lease expiring in 90 days, and the landlord wants a 20 percent rent increase to 1,800 a month. A smaller unit 400 metres away costs 1,100 but has less passing trade, and moving costs about 4,000. Online orders are 25 percent of sales and rising.

options.name: accept
options.text: Accept the increase and sign a three-year renewal

options.name: negotiate
options.text: Counter with a 7 percent increase and a one-year term

options.name: moveshop
options.text: Move to the smaller unit and reduce the stock on display

options.name: onlineonly
options.text: Close the shop and run the business as online only

options.name: popupmodel
options.text: Keep a small corner in a shared market hall and expand online

decision: How should the caterer scale a recipe for 400 guests?
context: A caterer has tested a braised dish for 20 and must serve 400 in 3 days. The ovens fit 60 portions per batch, rented bratt pans cost 180 a day, and the sauce reduces differently at scale. A tasting for the client is possible tomorrow.

options.name: ovenbatches
options.text: Cook in seven oven batches using the tested method

options.name: rentpans
options.text: Rent the bratt pans and adapt the recipe to larger volume

options.name: simplify
options.text: Switch to a simpler roast dish that scales reliably

options.name: splitkitchen
options.text: Cook half in the venue kitchen and half at the base

options.name: trialfirst
options.text: Run a 100-portion trial before choosing a method

decision: What should the dairy do after a cooling tank failure?
context: A dairy's milk cooling tank failed with 1,800 litres inside at 14 degrees and a tanker due in 5 hours. Ice from a nearby supplier costs 400, a neighbour offers 600 litres of tank space, and the rest could be pasteurised on site into cheese. The collection price is 0.40 per litre.

options.name: buyice
options.text: Buy ice and keep cooling the tank until the tanker arrives

options.name: neighbourtank
options.text: Move 600 litres to the neighbour's tank and ice the remainder

options.name: makecheese
options.text: Pasteurise the milk on site and turn it into cheese today

options.name: dumpmilk
options.text: Accept the loss and discard the milk to avoid quality risks

options.name: callvet
options.text: Call the tank engineer and wait for the diagnosis before acting

decision: How should the lab absorb a 15 percent budget cut?
context: A lab with a 400,000 annual budget loses 15 percent, mostly from consumables and a postdoc contract. Cutting one student's stipend is not allowed, the shared microscope service fee is 30,000, and two grants await a decision in 4 months.

options.name: dropservicef
options.text: Cancel the microscope service and use a partner's instrument

options.name: endcontract
options.text: Let the postdoc contract lapse at its natural end date

options.name: cutconsumables
options.text: Reduce consumables across all the projects evenly

options.name: pauseproject
options.text: Pause the lowest-priority project and reassign its funds

options.name: bridgeloan
options.text: Use departmental bridge money until the grants are decided

decision: How should the club plan the charity fun run route?
context: A club expects 800 runners for a 10 km event. The park loop is closed to traffic but narrow with pinch points, the river road is wide but needs a 3,500 road-closure permit, and a stadium track offers 25 laps with great spectator access but little scenery.

options.name: parkloop
options.text: Use the park loop and stagger the runners in start waves

options.name: riverroad
options.text: Pay for the river road closure and start everyone together

options.name: stadium
options.text: Hold the whole event on the stadium track, lap by lap

options.name: capentries
options.text: Keep the park loop and cap the entries at 500 runners

options.name: twoevents
options.text: Split it into a 5 km park run and a 10 km river run

decision: How should the bicycle workshop reduce its repair backlog?
context: A bicycle workshop has 45 bikes waiting at 5 per day capacity and a 9-day average wait. Hiring a part-time mechanic costs 1,400 a month, an express service at triple price could free capacity, and a few trainees from a youth scheme are available free but slower.

options.name: hirepart
options.text: Hire a part-time mechanic for the busy season ahead

options.name: express
options.text: Offer a priced express service and limit the standard slots

options.name: trainees
options.text: Take on the youth scheme trainees for the simpler jobs

options.name: triage
options.text: Triage the bikes and do quick fixes first, bigger jobs later

options.name: closebooking
options.text: Stop taking new bookings for two weeks to clear the queue

decision: How should the team handle a rising cloud bill?
context: A cloud bill rose from 6,000 to 9,500 a month in a year, mostly storage and idle test environments. Reserved capacity commitments could save 30 percent but lock in for 3 years, and shutting test environments at night saves about 900. The product roadmap may shift sharply in 8 months.

options.name: reserve
options.text: Commit to a three-year reservation on stable workloads

options.name: nightoff
options.text: Shut down test environments overnight and at weekends

options.name: storagetidy
options.text: Delete and archive old storage across all accounts

options.name: quotas
options.text: Set team budgets with automatic alerts and monthly review

options.name: movehost
options.text: Move the steady workloads to a cheaper hosting provider

decision: How should the family plan the two-week summer trip?
context: A family of four has 14 days and 4,000 to spend, with children aged 6 and 9. A beach resort costs 3,800 all-in, a self-catered countryside cottage costs 1,900 but needs car travel and meals, and a rail tour of three cities costs 3,300 with more planning and walking.

options.name: resort
options.text: Book the beach resort for the full two weeks

options.name: cottage
options.text: Rent the countryside cottage and plan day trips by car

options.name: railtour
options.text: Do the three-city rail tour with a few days in each

options.name: split
options.text: Spend one week at the cottage and one week at a beach

options.name: stayhome
options.text: Stay at home and fund a series of day excursions

decision: How should the local paper cover a council vote?
context: A local paper has one reporter free on a night when the council votes on a school closure, and a charity gala with a major donor happens the same evening. The council livestream will be public, the gala drives advertiser relations, and a freelance journalist is available at 120.

options.name: sendreporter
options.text: Send the reporter to the council meeting to cover the vote

options.name: sendgala
options.text: Send the reporter to the gala to please the advertisers

options.name: freelancer
options.text: Hire the freelancer for the gala and keep the reporter at council

options.name: livestream
options.text: Watch the livestream and publish a report the next morning

options.name: photoonly
options.text: Send a photographer to the gala and use a wire summary instead

decision: How should the adult evening class fill a vacant slot?
context: A community college has one free Tuesday evening slot and a room for 24. A language class has a waiting list of 31, a wood-joinery course has 12 interested but needs 900 for equipment, and an accounting basics class has a funded teacher but only 9 signups.

options.name: language
options.text: Run the language class and split the waiting list across terms

options.name: joinery
options.text: Run the joinery course and buy the extra equipment needed

options.name: accounting
options.text: Run the accounting class with its already funded teacher

options.name: alternate
options.text: Alternate the slot between language and joinery by term

options.name: survey
options.text: Survey local residents and decide on the slot next month

decision: Where should the food truck park on weekdays?
context: A food truck makes about 600 on a good lunch at the business park but pays a 90 daily pitch fee, and it makes 420 near the university with no fee but a 3-hour shorter window. An evening market pays 300 on average with a 40 pitch fee, and a brewery offers a free spot with a 15 percent revenue share.

options.name: businesspark
options.text: Park at the business park and accept the daily pitch fee

options.name: university
options.text: Park by the university and keep the lunch window shorter

options.name: eveningmarket
options.text: Work the evening market and skip the lunch service entirely

options.name: brewery
options.text: Take the brewery's free spot with its revenue share terms

options.name: rotate
options.text: Rotate between all the sites on different days of the week

decision: How should the village roll out smart water meters?
context: A village has 520 households with old meters, and leaks cause about 18 percent water loss. Smart meters cost 140 each installed, a leak-detection survey of the mains costs 25,000, and a pilot in one district of 80 homes would take 6 months. A water company grant covers 30 percent of any scheme.

options.name: allmeters
options.text: Install smart meters in all homes using the grant money

options.name: mainsurvey
options.text: Fund the mains leak survey first and repair what it finds

options.name: pilot
options.text: Pilot the meters in one district before any wider rollout

options.name: bothphased
options.text: Do the survey now and install the meters over three years

options.name: manualreads
options.text: Keep the old meters and have staff read them each month

decision: How should the meetup spend its 2,000 sponsorship?
context: A developer meetup has 2,000 from a sponsor for a year. It meets monthly with 35 attendees, the venue is free, and members ask for a bigger speaker, food at each event, or a full-day hackathon costing about 1,800. Attendance has fallen 20 percent over the last 6 months.

options.name: bigspeaker
options.text: Book one well-known external speaker for a flagship evening

options.name: foodeach
options.text: Provide food and drinks at every monthly meeting this year

options.name: hackathon
options.text: Run a full-day hackathon with most of the available funds

options.name: savefund
options.text: Hold the money in reserve for any unforeseen needs later

options.name: surveyfirst
options.text: Survey the members first and spend it on the top answer

decision: How should the family arrange care for a parent?
context: A parent aged 82 lives alone, 2 hours from the nearest child, and has had two falls this year. Home carers for 4 hours a day cost 1,500 a month, a care home place costs 3,600, and moving in with a child would mean a 40 minute commute each day. The parent wants to stay put.

options.name: homecare
options.text: Hire home carers for 4 hours a day at the parent's house

options.name: carehome
options.text: Arrange a place for the parent in a care home nearby

options.name: movein
options.text: Have the parent move in with the nearest of the children

options.name: monitor
options.text: Install fall sensors, with weekly visits and a daily phone call

options.name: trialstay
options.text: Arrange a trial stay in a care home before deciding further

decision: How should the brewery use a gap in its schedule?
context: A small brewery has a fermenter free for 3 weeks. A seasonal ale could sell 1,200 litres at 3 a litre, a rush wholesale order for lager from a pub chain pays 2.20 a litre for 2,000 litres, and cleaning and maintenance of the older tanks has been postponed for 4 months.

options.name: seasonal
options.text: Brew the seasonal ale for sale in the brewery's own taproom

options.name: lagerorder
options.text: Fill the lager order for the pub chain at the lower price

options.name: maintenance
options.text: Use the window to clean and service the older tanks at last

options.name: testbatch
options.text: Brew a small experimental batch and leave the rest idle

options.name: rentfermenter
options.text: Rent the free fermenter to a neighbouring brewery for a fee

decision: Who should start in the cup final?
context: A youth team coach must choose a goalkeeper for a final. One keeper has played all season and made 4 costly errors, another joined in January and has not conceded in 5 games, and a third is injured but recovering with a 70 percent chance of full fitness. Parents are paying attention to the decision.

options.name: regular
options.text: Start the regular keeper who has played all season long

options.name: newcomer
options.text: Start the January signing with the five clean sheets

options.name: recovering
options.text: Start the recovering keeper if he passes a late fitness test

options.name: rotatehalves
options.text: Play the regular keeper first half and the newcomer second

options.name: trainingvote
options.text: Pick whoever performs best in the final week of training

decision: How should the council respond to quarry noise complaints?
context: A quarry near 300 homes has generated 42 complaints in 3 months about early starts at 6 am. It employs 60 local people, and its permit allows a 6 am start. The council can negotiate hours, commission a noise study for 7,000, or open a formal review of the permit.

options.name: negotiate
options.text: Negotiate a voluntary 7 am start with the quarry operator

options.name: noisestudy
options.text: Commission the noise study before taking any firm position

options.name: review
options.text: Open a formal review of the quarry's operating permit

options.name: barrier
options.text: Ask the quarry to build an earth barrier and share the cost

options.name: residentpanel
options.text: Create a residents and quarry panel that meets each quarter

decision: How should the field team service its sensor network?
context: A research team has 45 weather sensors across a mountain valley and 9 have failed. A field trip costs about 1,800 and takes 4 days, local volunteers could swap units for a stipend but with weaker quality control, and a software fix might revive 4 of the 9 remotely.

options.name: fieldtrip
options.text: Send the team on a four-day trip to repair every failed unit

options.name: volunteers
options.text: Use local volunteers to swap out the failed sensors for pay

options.name: remotefix
options.text: Push the remote fix first and visit only the sites left over

options.name: acceptloss
options.text: Accept 36 working sensors and adjust the analysis to fit

options.name: waitseason
options.text: Wait for the planned summer trip and repair all units then

decision: How should the shop run its clearance sale?
context: A homeware shop has 900 units of old stock worth 14,000 at cost, and the shelf space is needed in 6 weeks for the new range. A 50 percent discount would recover about 60 percent of cost, a bulk sale to a liquidator recovers 35 percent at once, and a bundled offer may sell slower but at higher prices.

options.name: halfprice
options.text: Mark everything down 50 percent for a fixed 3-week sale

options.name: liquidator
options.text: Sell the whole lot to a liquidator now for a quick exit

options.name: bundles
options.text: Bundle slow items with popular ones at a smaller discount

options.name: staged
options.text: Cut prices in steps of 20 percent every second week

options.name: donatewrite
options.text: Donate the slowest half to charity and write off the loss

decision: How should the town prepare for spring flood risk?
context: A riverside town of 4,000 has flooded twice in 12 years, damaging 60 homes each time. Permanent barriers cost 1.2 million, demountable barriers 380,000 with 6 hours needed to erect, and upstream wetland restoration costs 650,000 with benefits that build over 8 years. The emergency budget holds 90,000.

options.name: permbarrier
options.text: Build permanent barriers along the most flood-prone stretch

options.name: demountable
options.text: Buy demountable barriers and train volunteers to erect them

options.name: wetland
options.text: Fund upstream wetland restoration to slow the river

options.name: homegrants
options.text: Give grants to the 60 homes for individual flood protection

options.name: earlywarning
options.text: Invest in a sensor network and an early warning alert system

options.name: relocate
options.text: Offer a voluntary buyout to the most exposed households

decision: What should the 5-person team hire next?
context: A five-person software team has 14 months of runway and a backlog of customer requests growing by 12 a month. Customers report slow support replies, one engineer carries most of the infrastructure knowledge, and a salesperson could add about 3 new accounts a month at 6,000 monthly cost.

options.name: engineer
options.text: Hire a senior engineer to share the infrastructure load

options.name: support
options.text: Hire a support specialist to cut the customer reply times

options.name: sales
options.text: Hire a salesperson to grow the base of paying accounts

options.name: contractor
options.text: Bring in a contractor for six months to work the backlog

options.name: nohire
options.text: Hire nobody and stretch the runway by a few more months

options.name: designer
options.text: Hire a product designer to simplify the requests at source

decision: How should the farm get its berries picked on time?
context: A berry farm has 12 hectares ripening in a 10-day window and normally uses 40 pickers. Only 26 have confirmed this year, a picking machine for half the area costs 11,000 to hire and bruises about 8 percent of fruit, and a late harvest loses roughly 15 percent of the crop per day.

options.name: recruitmore
options.text: Advertise locally for extra pickers at a higher piece rate

options.name: machinehire
options.text: Hire the picking machine for the half it suits best

options.name: pickyourown
options.text: Open half the fields as pick-your-own at a lower price

options.name: longerdays
options.text: Extend the daily hours for the 26 confirmed pickers

options.name: neighbours
options.text: Ask neighbouring farms to lend workers for later help in return

options.name: freezerline
options.text: Sell the part nobody can pick as a standing crop to a buyer

decision: How should the restaurant respond to rising ingredient costs?
context: A 40-seat restaurant has seen food costs rise from 31 to 38 percent of sales, with an average main course price of 19. Regulars complain loudly when prices rise, the most expensive dish is also the most popular, and a shorter menu could reduce waste by an estimated 6 percent.

options.name: raiseprices
options.text: Raise all menu prices by 7 percent and explain the reason

options.name: shortmenu
options.text: Shorten the menu to cut waste and ordering complexity

options.name: portions
options.text: Reduce portion sizes on the most expensive dishes served

options.name: cheaperswap
options.text: Substitute cheaper seasonal ingredients in the popular dishes

options.name: setmenu
options.text: Introduce a fixed-price set menu on weekdays for steadier covers

options.name: surcharge
options.text: Add a service charge and leave the menu prices unchanged

decision: How should the school fit in a new reading programme?
context: A primary school wants to introduce a 30-minute daily reading programme for 210 pupils starting after the autumn break, with 9 weeks to the end of term. The timetable is full, Year 6 is revising for tests, and a teaching assistant is on leave for 5 weeks. Evidence suggests gains build slowly.

options.name: startnow
options.text: Start immediately by shortening the afternoon lessons

options.name: startjanuary
options.text: Wait until January and prepare materials over the break

options.name: youngonly
options.text: Start with Years 1 to 3 and extend to others later

options.name: replacecircle
options.text: Replace the weekly assembly slot with reading sessions

options.name: volunteers
options.text: Recruit parent volunteers to run the sessions

options.name: pilotclass
options.text: Pilot in two classes and use the autumn results to adapt

decision: How should the lab acquire a mass spectrometer?
context: A lab needs a mass spectrometer for a 3-year project. Buying new costs 310,000, a refurbished unit costs 140,000 with a short warranty, a shared instrument at another university charges 60 an hour with queues of 2 weeks, and a commercial lab charges 90 a sample. About 4,000 samples are planned.

options.name: buynew
options.text: Buy the new instrument with a full service contract

options.name: refurbished
options.text: Buy the refurbished unit and budget for repairs

options.name: sharedunit
options.text: Book time on the university's shared instrument

options.name: commercial
options.text: Send samples to the commercial lab for analysis

options.name: coinvest
options.text: Co-purchase a new unit with a neighbouring department

options.name: leaseunit
options.text: Lease an instrument for the three years of the project

decision: How should the ice rink manage its energy costs?
context: A community ice rink pays 41,000 a year for electricity, up 35 percent in two years. A heat recovery system costs 55,000 and saves an estimated 9,000 a year, solar panels cost 70,000 and save 12,000 but only in summer, and closing for 6 weeks in summer saves 7,000 but loses a camp income of 11,000.

options.name: heatrecovery
options.text: Install the heat recovery system on the refrigeration plant

options.name: solar
options.text: Install solar panels on the roof of the rink building

options.name: summerclose
options.text: Close the rink for 6 weeks in the summer to save power

options.name: raiseticket
options.text: Raise ticket prices by 10 percent and change nothing else

options.name: fixedtariff
options.text: Negotiate a fixed multi-year electricity tariff with the supplier

options.name: ledgrant
options.text: Seek a green grant and wait a year before any investment

decision: How should the clinic move from paper records?
context: A rural clinic with 3 staff keeps 6,500 paper patient files and wants to digitise them. A scanning service costs 1.10 a file, a records system costs 1,200 a year, and staff scanning in quiet hours would take about 14 months. Power and internet drop out several times a month.

options.name: scanservice
options.text: Pay a scanning service to digitise everything in one go

options.name: staffscan
options.text: Scan files gradually in quiet hours with existing staff

options.name: newonly
options.text: Start digital records for new patients and leave old files

options.name: hybrid
options.text: Scan only the files of active patients seen in two years

options.name: offlinesystem
options.text: Choose an offline-capable system and sync when the internet works

options.name: delay
options.text: Wait a year until the connection is improved by the provider

decision: How should the scouts handle a camp with too few leaders?
context: A scout group has 42 children booked for a 5-day camp and only 5 qualified adult leaders where 7 are needed. Two parents are willing but untrained, a shorter 3-day camp needs only 4 leaders, and a partner group could merge with them but would add 20 children.

options.name: trainparents
options.text: Fast-track the two willing parents through basic leader training

options.name: shortcamp
options.text: Cut the camp to three days and keep the group as it is

options.name: merge
options.text: Merge with the partner group and share one leader team

options.name: capnumbers
options.text: Cap attendance at 30 children chosen by a fair lottery

options.name: splitcamps
options.text: Run two shorter camps for half of the children each time

options.name: daytrips
options.text: Replace the camp with a series of separate day trips

decision: What should the ops team do about repeated outages?
context: A regional ISP had three outages of about 2 hours each in a quarter, all on the same aggregation switch. Replacing the switch costs 28,000 and takes 6 weeks, adding a redundant link costs 9,000, and changing the vendor's firmware may fix the bug but has failed once before. The network serves 5,000 customers.

options.name: replaceswitch
options.text: Replace the faulty aggregation switch with a newer model

options.name: redundantlink
options.text: Add a redundant link to carry the traffic when the switch fails

options.name: firmware
options.text: Apply the vendor's firmware update during a night window

options.name: credits
options.text: Offer customers credits and keep monitoring, changing no hardware

options.name: splitload
options.text: Move half of the customers onto another aggregation switch

options.name: vendorescalate
options.text: Escalate to the vendor and hold off any spending for now

decision: How should the siblings handle their late parent's house?
context: Three siblings inherit a house valued at 360,000 in a market where prices are flat. One lives in the area and wants to keep it, one needs cash for a mortgage, and one lives abroad. Repairs of about 25,000 are needed before any sale, and renting it would bring 1,400 a month.

options.name: sellhouse
options.text: Sell the house after the repairs and split the proceeds

options.name: buyout
options.text: Let the local sibling buy out the others over 5 years

options.name: rentout
options.text: Rent the house out and share the income for a few years

options.name: sellasis
options.text: Sell as is at a discount to avoid the repair costs

options.name: partialrent
options.text: Let the local sibling rent it at a fair price and decide later

options.name: mediator
options.text: Hire a mediator and defer every decision for three months

decision: How should the rail operator revise its commuter timetable?
context: A regional line runs 4 trains an hour at peak and 2 off peak, carrying 9,000 passengers a day. Adding a fifth peak train needs a new unit costing 4 million, dropping a stop at a small town saves 3 minutes, and evening trains are only a third full. A union agreement limits changes to driver shifts.

options.name: fifthtrain
options.text: Lease the extra unit and run five peak trains an hour

options.name: skipstop
options.text: Skip the small town stop on the fast services at peak

options.name: lessevening
options.text: Cut evening trains and use the freed drivers at the peak

options.name: longertrains
options.text: Lengthen the existing peak trains instead of adding more

options.name: pricepeak
options.text: Raise peak fares to spread demand into the shoulder hours

options.name: keepas
options.text: Keep the timetable and publish live crowding data to riders

decision: How should the farmer hand over the farm?
context: A farmer aged 66 has two children, one who has worked on the farm for 12 years and one who lives in the city and holds a legal share. The farm is worth about 1.8 million, mostly land, and a part sale to a neighbour is possible. Inheritance tax rules will change in two years.

options.name: transferfarm
options.text: Transfer the whole farm to the working child now

options.name: equalshare
options.text: Split the farm into equal shares between both children

options.name: sellneighbour
options.text: Sell the land to the neighbour and divide the proceeds

options.name: company
options.text: Create a company with both children as shareholders

options.name: leaseback
options.text: Lease the land to the working child and keep ownership

options.name: delaywill
options.text: Keep the farm and settle it through a will later

decision: How should the library reach new readers?
context: A library has lost 15 percent of its members in 3 years and has 20,000 for outreach. A book van costs 18,000 for the first year, school partnerships cost 6,000 and staff time, a late-night opening costs 5,500, and a digital lending app costs 8,000 a year but has low use among the over 60s.

options.name: bookvan
options.text: Run a book van to housing estates and to care homes

options.name: schools
options.text: Build school partnerships with class visits and library cards

options.name: lateopening
options.text: Open late on two nights a week for working adults

options.name: digitalapp
options.text: Launch a digital lending app and promote it online

options.name: amnesty
options.text: Offer a fines amnesty alongside a membership drive in town

options.name: pooledfund
options.text: Split the money across a small version of each option

decision: How should the festival choose its opening film?
context: A small film festival with 600 seats has three options for the opening night: a crowd-pleasing comedy likely to sell out, a critically praised documentary with a filmmaker attending, and a local student feature with 40 cast and crew who would bring family. Sponsors prefer the comedy.

options.name: comedy
options.text: Open with the crowd-pleasing comedy for a sold-out night

options.name: documentary
options.text: Open with the documentary and the filmmaker's live Q and A

options.name: localfilm
options.text: Open with the local student feature and its large cast crowd

options.name: doublebill
options.text: Show the local short and the comedy together as a double bill

options.name: votefilm
options.text: Let ticket buyers vote online for the opening night film

options.name: opendoc
options.text: Open with the documentary and move the comedy to closing night

decision: How should the glassworks replace its furnace?
context: A glassworks has a furnace that is 15 years old, uses 28 percent more gas than a new model, and has cracked once. A new furnace costs 90,000 and needs a 3-week shutdown, a rebuild costs 38,000 with a 10-day shutdown, and an electric furnace costs 120,000 but exposes the shop to power prices.

options.name: newgas
options.text: Install a new gas furnace during a three-week shutdown

options.name: rebuild
options.text: Rebuild the existing furnace and add better insulation

options.name: electric
options.text: Install the electric furnace and sign a fixed power contract

options.name: rentcapacity
options.text: Rent time at another studio while the shop is shut down

options.name: repairnow
options.text: Patch the crack and run the old furnace for one more year

options.name: shrinkshop
options.text: Downsize to a smaller furnace and make a narrower range

decision: How should the community garden manage its water?
context: A community garden with 36 plots pays 1,900 a year for mains water that has doubled since last year. A rainwater tank system costs 4,500 and covers roughly half of the demand, a well drilling costs 8,000 with uncertain yield, and plot mulching schemes could cut demand by 20 percent for little cost.

options.name: tanks
options.text: Install the rainwater tank system on the shed roofs

options.name: welldrill
options.text: Drill a well and test how much water it will yield

options.name: mulch
options.text: Require mulching on every plot and teach the method

options.name: meterplots
options.text: Meter each plot and bill members for what they use

options.name: droughtcrops
options.text: Shift the planting rules toward drought-tolerant crops

options.name: councilask
options.text: Ask the council for a reduced water rate for community use

decision: How should the ward fix its night shift rota?
context: A hospital ward with 22 nurses has 5 unfilled night shifts a week and two resignations citing nights. Agency cover costs double, a night premium of 15 percent would cost 45,000 a year, and a permanent night team would require moving 4 nurses out of day shifts, which two of them oppose.

options.name: agency
options.text: Fill the night gaps with agency nurses for the time being

options.name: premium
options.text: Introduce the 15 percent night premium for all night staff

options.name: nightteam
options.text: Form a permanent night team, asking for volunteers first

options.name: shorterblock
options.text: Move everyone to shorter blocks of consecutive night shifts

options.name: floatpool
options.text: Create a float pool of nurses shared across several wards

options.name: reducebeds
options.text: Close four beds overnight to match the available staffing

decision: How long should the team keep old log data?
context: A team stores 14 TB of application logs, costing 700 a month, with 12 months retained. Security analysts want 24 months for investigations, a legal requirement may set 6 months for personal data, and querying data older than 3 months takes minutes rather than seconds.

options.name: sixmonths
options.text: Cut retention to 6 months across all of the log sources

options.name: twelvemonths
options.text: Keep the current 12 months and revisit after the legal review

options.name: twentyfour
options.text: Extend to 24 months for security logs and 6 for the rest

options.name: tiered
options.text: Move old logs to cheap cold storage with slow search

options.name: sampled
options.text: Keep full logs for 3 months and sampled logs after that

options.name: anonymise
options.text: Strip the personal fields and keep anonymised logs for 24 months

decision: How should the couple choose their wedding setup?
context: A couple has 12,000 and a guest list of 110, with 3 months to plan. A rented barn costs 4,500 but needs catering and toilets hired in, a hotel package costs 9,800 for 80 guests, and a registry office plus a restaurant meal for 40 costs 5,200. Both families live far apart.

options.name: barn
options.text: Hire the barn and arrange the catering and toilets themselves

options.name: hotel
options.text: Book the hotel package and trim the guest list to 80

options.name: smallmeal
options.text: Hold a small ceremony followed by a meal for 40 people

options.name: twoevents
options.text: Marry quietly and host a casual party for everyone later

options.name: delayyear
options.text: Postpone for a year to save more and plan in detail

options.name: travelhome
options.text: Hold two small parties, one near each side of the family

decision: How should the mill restore its water wheel?
context: A heritage mill's water wheel is rotting and a full restoration costs 85,000, of which a heritage fund may provide 50 percent if approved in 9 months. A cheaper replica in steel costs 40,000, and a partial repair costs 18,000 and lasts maybe 5 years. The mill earns 30,000 a year from visitors.

options.name: fullrestore
options.text: Wait for the fund decision and do the full restoration

options.name: steelreplica
options.text: Build the steel replica now without waiting for the fund

options.name: partial
options.text: Do the partial repair now and apply for the fund meanwhile

options.name: staticdisplay
options.text: Retire the wheel as a static display and use the money elsewhere

options.name: crowdfund
options.text: Run a crowdfunding appeal to bring the match funding forward

options.name: phasedwork
options.text: Restore the wheel in two phases across two separate seasons

decision: How should the cheese stall fill its empty weekday slot?
context: A market stall holds a licence for Thursdays that it has not used, and the market charges 45 per day whether it trades or not. Past Thursday trials took 150 on average, the stall's best day is Saturday at 520, and the owner has 6 free hours that day-job rules otherwise restrict.

options.name: thursday
options.text: Trade on Thursdays with the same range as Saturday

options.name: sublet
options.text: Sublet the Thursday licence to another trader for a fee

options.name: giveup
options.text: Give up the Thursday licence and save the daily charge

options.name: special
options.text: Run a themed Thursday with tastings and a smaller range

options.name: onlinepick
options.text: Use Thursdays for online order pickups at the stall

options.name: lunchcart
options.text: Use the slot to sell hot toasties to the lunch crowd
